name: veterinary_clinic_system_028_draft_invoice_purge
instruction: Purge every draft billing document from both the invoice and estimate ledgers. A 'draft' status means the document is not yet authoritative and should be removed. For each deleted draft invoice or estimate, push one outbound email communications row to that document's owner: channel='email', direction='outbound', subject='Draft document cancelled <batch_code>', body='Draft <invoice_number or estimate_number> has been removed from our system.', logged_by='Billing', occurred_at the episode timestamp, owner_id set to the document's owner_id, and patient_id set to the document's patient_id. After the purge, push one ops_reports row with report='draft_purge' and the live batch_code containing: episode_date, invoices_deleted, estimates_deleted, total_deleted, affected_owners (sorted list of distinct owner_id strings), affected_patients (sorted list of distinct patient_id strings), affected_documents (list of {type, document_number, owner_id, patient_id, location_id} for every deleted document, sorted by document_number), and location_breakdown (dict mapping each location name to the count of deleted documents from that location). Leave every non-draft invoice and estimate byte-identical to the seed snapshot. If a draft_purge report or cancellation communications for this batch already exist, overwrite them so the result is idempotent.

success_criteria.summary: All draft billing_invoices and billing_estimates are deleted; every non-draft row in those collections is byte-identical to the seed snapshot. One cancellation communication is pushed per deleted document with exact subject/body/occurred_at and correct owner_id/patient_id. Exactly one ops_reports 'draft_purge' row for this batch contains the live counts, sorted affected owner/patient lists, the affected_documents detail, and a location breakdown. Every aggregate (counts, distinct counts, location counts) is computed two independent ways (raw-row Python and SQL) and must agree with the agent's written report. All collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical to the seed snapshot.

checks.expect: No draft invoice remains; all non-draft invoices byte-identical to seed snapshot
No draft estimate remains; all non-draft estimates byte-identical to seed snapshot
One cancellation communication per deleted draft document with exact fields
Exactly one 'draft_purge' row for this batch with all required fields
deleted invoice count and location breakdown agree between raw-row Python and SQL
deleted estimate count and location breakdown agree between raw-row Python and SQL

hazards: The draft ledgers are small: exactly 1 draft invoice (INV-1003, owner 3, patient 3, location 3, total $546.00) and 30 draft estimates. The bulk of the collections are non-draft (257 paid/sent/overdue invoices and 70 sent/accepted/declined estimates). A solution that deletes non-draft rows fails the canary byte-identity checks; a solution that does not delete the estimate drafts leaves 30 stale rows.

The cancellation communications must be one per deleted document, not one per affected owner. Each of the 31 deleted documents has a distinct owner and patient in this seed, but the code must not collapse by owner.
The report's affected_owners and affected_patients must be the distinct, sorted owner/patient ids from the deleted documents. A list that includes all owners or uses the document ids fails.
The location_breakdown must use locations.name, not the raw location_id. The three locations are Main Street Animal Hospital, Riverside Veterinary Clinic, and Cedar Park Animal Care Center.

On a second run there are no draft documents left. A naive re-run that purges live drafts and then pushes communications would create zero new rows and a wrong report. The gold uses an idempotent overwrite keyed by batch_code.
